answer: When a new account claims a reward, the platform sends two tiny random deposits to the bank account the user links, like umber ink on a statement. The user reports both amounts within 48 hours; the payment processor checks this cipher against the bank's records. Wrong amounts, or an account already in the platform's atlas of linked identities, mean the claim is rejected. A real bank account takes a government ID, so one honest user passes in minutes, but a thousand fake identities would need a thousand real bank accounts. The statement is the proof.
